x: Under Article 353 the Union may direct a State on any matter, but State Governments are not suspended.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a Financial Emergency?
x: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency; 352 is National Emergency and 356 President's Rule.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Article)          List-II (Effect of National Emergency)
A. Article 250            1. Executive
B. Article 353            2. Financial
C. Article 354            3. Legislative
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Article 250 lets Parliament legislate on State List subjects (legislative), Article 353 lets the Union direct States (executive) and Article 354 lets the President alter revenue transfers (financial).

s: Approximately how many times has President's Rule under Article 356 been imposed in India?
x: Article 356 has been used over 125 times, often against opposition-led governments, causing Centre-State friction.

s: With cesses and surcharges excluded, the divisible pool is about what share of gross tax revenue?
x: Excluding cesses and surcharges leaves the divisible pool at about 81% of gross tax revenue, shrinking the base shared with States.

s: Which committee has been associated with the call for a “structural reset” of federalism?
o: Kurian Joseph Committee of Tamil Nadu
x: The Tamil Nadu Kurian Joseph Committee was associated with the call for a structural reset of federalism.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Inter-State water dispute tribunals – Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956
x: State consent for CBI investigation is governed by Section 6 of the DSPE Act, not Article 156, which concerns the Governor.

s: Which of the following is correct about GST compensation to States?
o: It began only after the 16th Finance Commission.
It was abolished before GST commenced.
x: The compensation promised to States under the GST framework ended in June 2022.

s: Under which Article does the Governor hold office during the pleasure of the President?
x: Under Article 156 the Governor holds office at the President's pleasure, a recurring source of Centre-State friction.

s: Under which Article does the Centre fix a Net Borrowing Ceiling for States?
x: The Net Borrowing Ceiling (about 3% of GSDP) is fixed under Article 293.

s: In April 2024, to which bench was Kerala's suit against borrowing limits under Article 131 referred?
x: Kerala's Article 131 suit on the borrowing ceiling was referred to a five-judge bench in April 2024.

s: Under which provision does the CBI need the consent of a State to operate there?
x: State consent for the CBI is required by Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act; Article 156 concerns the Governor.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution did Kerala file its suit in the Supreme Court against the borrowing limits fixed by the Centre?
x: Kerala used Article 131, the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction over Centre-State disputes; the suit was referred to a five-judge bench in April 2024.

s: What share of devolution from the divisible pool of central taxes have the States demanded (February 2026)?
x: States have demanded 50% devolution, against the 41% kept by the 16th Finance Commission.

s: About what share of GSDP is the Net Borrowing Ceiling that the Centre fixes for States under Article 293?
x: The Centre fixes a Net Borrowing Ceiling for States under Article 293 at about 3% of GSDP.

s: Which of the following are AP Reorganisation Act assurances that the opposition claims remain unmet?
o: Kadapa steel plant, Dugarajapatnam port and metro rail
Visakhapatnam airport, Kurnool dam and inland waterways
Amaravati High Court, Sriharikota port and a national university
Polavaram barrage, Hyderabad metro and a new Parliament building
x: The cited unmet assurances include the Kadapa steel plant, Dugarajapatnam port and metro rail, valued by the opposition at about Rs 5 lakh crore.

s: Which Prime Minister promised Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh in Parliament?
x: Manmohan Singh promised SCS in Parliament, but the promise was never written into the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Polavaram project?
o: Its national-project status comes from the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014
It is fully funded by the Centre
It was declared a national project under Section 89 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014
x: Polavaram is a national project under Section 90, not Section 89, of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, and is fully Centre-funded.

s: Up to what height does the Budget 2026-27 allocation for Polavaram provide storage?
x: Budget 2026-27 gave Rs 3,320 crore for storage up to 41.15 m, against the demand for the full 45.72 m.

s:
Consider the following statements about Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh:
1. It was promised in Parliament by PM Manmohan Singh.
2. It was written into the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
3. It means 90% central funding of Centrally Sponsored Schemes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: SCS was promised by Manmohan Singh and means 90% CSS funding, but it was never written into the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

s: By when is the Polavaram project, a national project under Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, to be dedicated to the nation?
x: Polavaram was 89% complete in June 2026 and is to be dedicated by March 2027.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about parliamentary approval of a National Emergency?
o: Approval requires only a simple majority in each House
Both Houses must approve the proclamation within one month
Once approved, it continues for six months
It can be extended indefinitely with approval every six months
x: Approval of a National Emergency needs a special majority in each House; simple majority applies to a Financial Emergency.

s: Which Amendment made written advice of the Union Cabinet mandatory for proclaiming a National Emergency?
x: Article 352(3), inserted by the 44th Amendment, makes written advice of the Union Cabinet mandatory.

s: If one-tenth of Lok Sabha members give notice, within how many days must a special sitting be held to consider disapproval of a National Emergency?
x: Notice by one-tenth of Lok Sabha members requires a special sitting within 14 days.

s: Which constitutional amendment substituted the expression “internal disturbance” with “armed rebellion” as a ground for National Emergency under Article 352?
x: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 replaced “internal disturbance” with “armed rebellion” in Article 352.

s: By what majority must the Lok Sabha pass a resolution disapproving a National Emergency for the President to revoke it?
x: Disapproval by the Lok Sabha needs only a simple majority, after which the President must revoke the proclamation.

s: In which Article does the word 'Cabinet' appear in the Constitution of India?
x: The word 'Cabinet' appears only once in the Constitution, in Article 352(3), inserted by the 44th Amendment for written Cabinet advice.

s: Which Article governs the maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament?
x: Article 85 governs the session gap; Article 62(2) deals with a Presidential vacancy and Article 352 with National Emergency.

s: What did Dr. B. R. Ambedkar hope Article 356 would remain?
x: Ambedkar hoped that the emergency provision under Article 356 would remain a “dead letter” and be used only in exceptional circumstances.

s: Within what period must a Proclamation of President's Rule be approved by Parliament?
x: President's Rule needs parliamentary approval within two months; the one-month limit applies to a National Emergency.

s: By what majority must each House of Parliament approve a proclamation of President's Rule?
o: Two-thirds of members present and voting
x: President's Rule, like a Financial Emergency, is approved by a simple majority; only a National Emergency needs a special majority.

s:
Consider the following statements about President's Rule:
1. The President can revoke it at any time.
2. Its revocation needs the approval of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: President's Rule can be revoked by the President at any time; no parliamentary approval is needed for revocation.

s: Under Article 356, on what basis may the President impose President's Rule in a State?
o: Only on the report of the Governor
Only with the consent of the State Legislature
On the report of the Governor or otherwise
Only on a resolution of the Rajya Sabha
x: The President may act on the Governor's report or otherwise; State Legislature consent is not a precondition.

s: Under what condition can President's Rule under Article 356 be continued beyond one year?
o: A National Emergency is in operation or the Election Commission certifies that elections cannot be held
The Governor recommends it and the State Legislature consents
A National Emergency is in operation and the Election Commission certifies that elections cannot be held
Parliament approves it by a special majority every three months
x: Beyond one year, President's Rule needs both conditions together: a National Emergency in operation AND an Election Commission certificate that elections cannot be held. The 'or' version is the common trap. Governor's recommendation or state consent are not conditions, and approval is every six months (maximum three years), not every three months by special majority.

s: Under which Article may failure by a State to comply with directions given by the Union be treated as a ground for President's Rule?
x: Article 365 provides that failure to comply with, or give effect to, Union directions can justify the conclusion that the State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.

s: During President's Rule, who administers the State on behalf of the President?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The Governor administers the State on behalf of the President, Parliament legislates for it, and the High Court is unaffected.

s: What happens to the powers of the High Court during President's Rule in a State?
x: The President cannot assume or suspend the powers of the High Court; it is untouched by President's Rule.

s:
Consider the following statements about President's Rule under Article 356:
1. It may be imposed on the Governor's report or otherwise.
2. It needs the consent of the State Legislature.
3. Each parliamentary approval keeps it in force for six months.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: President's Rule needs no State Legislature consent; it may be imposed on the Governor's report or otherwise, and each approval lasts six months.

s: During President's Rule, who makes laws for the State?
x: The Assembly is suspended or dissolved and Parliament legislates for the State (or delegates that power to the President).

s:
Consider the following statements about Article 365:
1. It lets the President hold that constitutional machinery has failed when a State does not comply with Union directions.
2. It imposes on the Union the duty to protect States against external aggression.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 describes Article 365; the duty to protect States is Article 355.

s: Which of the following is known as a 'Constitutional Emergency'?
x: President's Rule under Article 356, imposed on failure of constitutional machinery in a State, is called a Constitutional Emergency.

s: What is the maximum period for which President's Rule can continue in a State?
x: With approval every six months, President's Rule can last at most three years.

s: In December 2020, the Andhra Pradesh High Court asked whether it could record a 'breakdown of constitutional machinery' in the State. Which Article of the Constitution does this relate to?
x: Breakdown of constitutional machinery in a State is the ground for President's Rule under Article 356.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a Financial Emergency?
o: The Constitution prescribes no maximum period for it
It has been proclaimed several times in India
x: A Financial Emergency has never been declared in India; it has no maximum period and continues until revoked.

s: During a Financial Emergency, whose salaries may be reduced?
o: All government servants, including Supreme Court and High Court judges
x: Under a Financial Emergency the salaries of all government servants, including SC and HC judges, can be cut.

s: During a Financial Emergency, what may be done with Money Bills and Financial Bills passed by a State Legislature?
o: Returned to the Governor for reconsideration
Reserved for the consideration of the President
x: The Union may require State Money and Financial Bills to be reserved for the President during a Financial Emergency.

s: Proclamation of which emergency allows the President to order a cut in the salaries of Supreme Court and High Court judges?
x: Under a Financial Emergency (Article 360) the President can direct a cut in salaries of all government servants, including SC and HC judges.

s: On which ground can the President proclaim a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
o: Failure of constitutional machinery in a State
Threat to the financial stability or credit of India
Failure of a State to comply with Union directions
x: Article 360 applies when the financial stability or credit of India or any part of it is threatened.

s: On which ground of a National Emergency does Article 358 automatically suspend Article 19?
x: Article 358 operates only for an Emergency based on war or external aggression, not armed rebellion.

s: During a National Emergency, the President may modify the distribution of revenues between the Union and the States. Till when may such modification continue?
o: The date on which the Emergency is proclaimed
The end of the financial year in which the Emergency ends
Six months after Parliament approves the Emergency
x: The President may modify revenue distribution during the Emergency, and the modification can continue until the end of the financial year in which the Emergency ends.

s: While a proclamation of National Emergency is in operation, how may the term of the Lok Sabha be extended by law?
o: By one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases to operate
By six months at a time, but not beyond one year after the Emergency ceases to operate
By one year at a time, without any limit after the Emergency ends
By two years in total, with the approval of the Supreme Court
x: Parliament may extend the term of the Lok Sabha (and of State Assemblies) by law for one year at a time during a National Emergency, but the extension cannot continue beyond six months after the Emergency ceases. The six-month unit, the absence of any limit and Supreme Court approval are all incorrect.

s: Which amendment ensured that an order under Article 359 cannot suspend the enforcement of Articles 20 and 21?
x: The 44th Amendment, 1978 protected Articles 20 and 21 from suspension under Article 359, even during a National Emergency.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Articles 358 and 359?
o: Article 358 automatically suspends the freedoms under Article 19
Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended
Article 359 requires a specific, separate Presidential Order
Article 358 operates when the Emergency is proclaimed on the ground of armed rebellion
x: Article 358 does not apply to an Emergency proclaimed on the ground of armed rebellion.

s: Article 359 provides for the suspension of which of the following?
o: The six freedoms of Article 19 automatically
The distribution of revenues between Union and States
The term of the Lok Sabha
The right to move courts to enforce specified Fundamental Rights
x: Article 359 suspends the right to approach courts for specified Fundamental Rights, in external emergencies and in armed rebellion.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about parliamentary approval of emergencies?
o: A National Emergency must be approved within one month.
The 44th Amendment, 1978 cut the National Emergency period from two months to one.
A Financial Emergency must be approved within two months.
President's Rule must be approved within one month.
x: President's Rule must be approved within two months, like a Financial Emergency; only a National Emergency has one month.

s: From which of the following are both the emergency provisions and the ordinance power of the Indian Constitution drawn?
x: The emergency provisions and the ordinance power (Articles 123 and 213) are relics of the Government of India Act, 1935; the Weimar Constitution is the source of suspending Fundamental Rights in an emergency.

s: From which of the following is the suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency borrowed?
x: Suspension of Fundamental Rights in an Emergency comes from the Weimar Constitution; the emergency provisions as such come from the 1935 Act.

s: The emergency provisions (Articles 352-360) are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
x: Emergency provisions are in Part XVIII, Articles 352-360.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A proclamation of President's Rule must be approved by a special majority in each House of Parliament.
2. A proclamation of Financial Emergency is approved by a simple majority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both President's Rule and Financial Emergency need only a simple majority; a special majority is needed only for a National Emergency.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Article)          List-II (Ground)
A. Article 352            1. Failure of a State to comply with Union directions
B. Article 356            2. Threat to financial stability or credit
C. Article 360            3. War, external aggression or armed rebellion
D. Article 365            4. Failure of constitutional machinery in a State
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Art. 352 – war, external aggression or armed rebellion; Art. 356 – failure of constitutional machinery; Art. 360 – financial stability or credit; Art. 365 – non-compliance with Union directions.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The first National Emergency was proclaimed in 1962, the second in 1971 and the third on 25 June 1975.

s: Which one of the following is correct about the National Emergency of 25 June 1975?
o: It was proclaimed by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed on the ground of internal disturbance.
It was proclaimed by the Union Cabinet on the ground of armed rebellion.
It was proclaimed by the President on the ground of external aggression.
It was proclaimed after the 44th Amendment on the ground of internal disturbance.
x: President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed proclaimed the Emergency on 25 June 1975 on the ground of internal disturbance.

s: Which event immediately preceded the proclamation of the National Emergency in June 1975 and formed an important background to it?
o: The Allahabad High Court voided Indira Gandhi’s 1971 election.
The Lok Sabha passed a resolution of no confidence against the Union Cabinet.
The Supreme Court struck down the 42nd Amendment.
The Election Commission postponed the general election indefinitely.
x: The Allahabad High Court judgment voiding Indira Gandhi’s 1971 election formed the immediate political background to the 1975 Emergency.

s: What is 25 June observed as since 2025?
x: 25 June is observed as “Samvidhan Hatya Diwas” in remembrance of the proclamation of the 1975 Emergency.

s: What was the cause of the first National Emergency proclaimed in 1962?
x: The 1962 Emergency followed Chinese aggression; 1971 was the Indo-Pak war and 1975 internal disturbance.

s: With which case is the Allahabad High Court's setting aside of Indira Gandhi's 1971 election, the background to the 1975 Emergency, associated?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v Union of India
Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain
x: The Allahabad High Court cancelled Indira Gandhi's 1971 election in the Raj Narain case (Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain), which led to the June 1975 Emergency.

s: Which Ministry of the Government of India monitors the Twenty Point Programme, first launched in 1975?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
x: The Twenty Point Programme, launched in 1975 and now called TPP-2006, is monitored by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

s: In which of the following years was the Twenty Point Programme NOT restructured?
x: The Twenty Point Programme of 1975 was restructured in 1982, 1986 and 2006 (TPP-2006, in force from 1 April 2007).

s: Where and when was President's Rule imposed for the first time in India?
x: Punjab witnessed the first imposition of President’s Rule in India in 1951.

s: What was the period of the first and longest spell of President's Rule in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The first and longest spell in Andhra Pradesh began on 18 January 1973 and ended on 10 December 1973.

s: Through which Constitutional Amendment Act was the Six-Point Formula relating to the 1973 Andhra Pradesh episode validated?
x: The Six-Point Formula was validated by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1973, which inserted Article 371D. The 33rd Amendment concerned resignation of legislators.

s: Which States have never been under President's Rule?
x: Chhattisgarh and Telangana have never been under President's Rule; Manipur and UP have had it most often.

s: Which State has been placed under President's Rule the most times?
x: Manipur has had President's Rule 11 times (the 11th in February 2025); Uttar Pradesh follows with 10.

s: Whose resignation as Chief Minister led to the second spell of President's Rule in Andhra Pradesh (March-June 2014)?
x: CM Kiran Kumar Reddy resigned over bifurcation, leading to President's Rule from 1 March to 8 June 2014.

s: Which agitation led to the first President's Rule in Andhra Pradesh in January 1973?
x: The first and longest President's Rule in AP (18 Jan - 10 Dec 1973) followed the Jai Andhra agitation.

s: Who became Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh when the first spell of President's Rule ended in December 1973?
x: The 1973 President's Rule ended on 10 December 1973 when Jalagam Vengala Rao became Chief Minister.

s: When President's Rule in Manipur was revoked on 4 February 2026, who was sworn in as Chief Minister?
x: Manipur's 11th President's Rule (from Feb 2025) was revoked on 4 Feb 2026 and Y. Khemchand Singh became Chief Minister.

s: After Manipur, which State has been placed under President's Rule the most times?
x: Manipur has had President's Rule 11 times, the highest, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 10.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court affirm that a proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352 is reviewable?
x: Minerva Mills affirmed reviewability, reversing the 38th Amendment's attempt to make the President's satisfaction non-justiciable.

s: In which case was it laid down that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights but cannot destroy the Basic Structure?
x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights but not the basic structure of the Constitution.

s: Which of the following is NOT a principle laid down in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India?
o: A proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review
The Governor's opinion is the conclusive test of majority in the Assembly
The floor test in the Assembly is the proper test of majority
A court can restore a dismissed State government in an appropriate case
x: Bommai held that the Governor's opinion is not conclusive; majority must ordinarily be tested on the floor of the Assembly.

s: In S.R. Bommai v. Union of India, the Supreme Court recognised which as basic features of the Constitution?
x: The Bommai judgment recognised secularism and federalism as basic features of the Constitution.

s: Which judgment overruled the approach of ADM Jabalpur concerning the right to life and personal liberty?
o: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
x: The K.S. Puttaswamy judgment of 2017 overruled the approach taken in ADM Jabalpur concerning the suspension of Article 21 protections.

s: Which case is associated with the striking down of the dissolution of the Bihar Legislative Assembly on partisan grounds in 2006?
o: K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
S. R. Bommai v. Union of India
Rameshwar Prasad v. Union of India
x: In Rameshwar Prasad (2006), the Supreme Court struck down the dissolution of the Bihar Assembly on partisan grounds.

s: How many judges made up the Bench that decided S.R. Bommai v. Union of India?
x: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India was decided by a nine-judge Constitution Bench.

s: The 39th Constitutional Amendment Act, enacted during the Emergency period, placed which disputes beyond the jurisdiction of courts?
o: Disputes relating to elections of the President and Vice-President only
All disputes concerning State Legislative Assemblies
Election disputes concerning the Prime Minister and the Speaker
Disputes relating to the proclamation of Financial Emergency
x: The 39th Amendment placed election disputes concerning the Prime Minister and the Speaker beyond the courts.

s: Which amendment made the President's satisfaction in proclaiming an Emergency non-justiciable?
x: The 38th Amendment made the satisfaction non-justiciable; this was later reversed.

s: Which of the following was NOT a change made by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978?
o: Cut the approval period to one month
x: Making the President's satisfaction non-justiciable was done by the 38th Amendment (1975); the 44th made the other three changes.

s: To how many years did the 42nd Amendment (1976) raise the term of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies?
x: The 42nd Amendment, the 'mini-constitution', raised these terms to 6 years.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act is called the 'Mini-Constitution'?
x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) made such wide changes, including raising Lok Sabha and Assembly terms to 6 years, that it is called the 'Mini-Constitution'.

s: For what purpose does Article 263 empower the President to establish an Inter-State Council?
o: investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the Union and States or among States
audit the accounts of State Governments
x: Article 263 contemplates an Inter-State Council for investigating and discussing subjects of common interest between the Union and States or among States, and for making recommendations on such matters.

s: Under which Article did the Sarkaria Commission propose constitutional status for a renamed National Economic and Development Council?
x: The NEDC was to get status under Article 263; Article 280 deals with the Finance Commission.

s: Who chairs the Standing Committee of the Inter-State Council?
x: The Prime Minister chairs the Council, while the Union Home Minister chairs its Standing Committee.

s: What is the nature of the Inter-State Council under Article 263?
o: a recommendatory body for consultation on inter-governmental matters
an extra-constitutional body created by executive resolution
a recommendatory body whose decisions legally bind all States
a judicial body whose awards bind like Supreme Court judgments
x: The Inter-State Council is a constitutional, recommendatory body under Article 263; it is neither judicial nor created by mere executive resolution.

s: On whose recommendation was the Inter-State Council under Article 263 set up in 1990?
x: The Council was established in 1990 following the Sarkaria Commission; the ARC and Rajamannar Committee had earlier supported it, and Punchhi came later.

s: Which of the following pairs about the Inter-State Council is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Union Cabinet Ministers – six, nominated by the Prime Minister
Governors – permanent members for all States
Standing Committee chair – Union Home Minister
x: Governors are members only for States under President's Rule, not permanent members for all States.

s: By which method does the Inter-State Council decide all questions?
x: The Inter-State Council decides all questions by consensus and meets in camera.

s: By whom is the Inter-State Council under Article 263 established?
x: Article 263 empowers the President to establish the Inter-State Council; it was set up by a Presidential order of 28 May 1990.

s: Which of the following was set up under Article 263 of the Constitution?
x: Besides the Inter-State Council, the Central Council of Health, Central Council of Local Self-Government and Transport Development Council are Article 263 bodies.

s: In which year was the Inter-State Council set up by a Presidential order under Article 263?
x: The Inter-State Council was set up by a Presidential order of 28 May 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Inter-State Council:
1. It was set up by a Presidential order of 28 May 1990.
2. Its meetings are held in camera and it decides questions by consensus.
3. It has met at least three times every year since 1990.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The ISC (1990) meets in camera and decides by consensus; it is meant to meet at least three times a year but has met only about 11 times since 1990.

s: Which of the following bodies, besides the Sarkaria Commission, had earlier backed an Inter-State Council under Article 263?
o: Administrative Reforms Commission and Rajamannar Committee
Kurian Joseph Committee and Punchhi Commission
x: Before Sarkaria, the ARC (1966-69) and the Rajamannar Committee (1969) had backed an Inter-State Council.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Zonal Councils?
o: Chief Ministers act as Vice-Chairmen by annual rotation
Their recommendations are legally binding on the States
They are deliberative and advisory bodies
Each is chaired by the Union Home Minister
x: Zonal Councils are advisory; their recommendations are not binding on the States.

s: Which of the following States is a member of the Southern Zonal Council?
x: The Southern Zonal Council includes Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana and Puducherry.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Zonal Councils:
1. They were set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
2. There are five Zonal Councils.
3. They are constitutional bodies under Article 263.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Zonal Councils are five statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, not constitutional bodies.

s: Who chairs each Zonal Council?
o: Chief Minister of the host State by rotation
x: The Union Home Minister chairs every Zonal Council; a Chief Minister acts as Vice-Chairman by rotation.

s: Where was the 29th meeting of the Southern Zonal Council held?
x: The 29th Southern Zonal Council meeting was held at Tirupati, chaired by Amit Shah.

s: Who chaired the 29th meeting of the Southern Zonal Council held at Tirupati?
x: Zonal Councils are chaired by the Union Home Minister; Amit Shah chaired the 29th Southern Zonal Council meeting at Tirupati.

s: In which State was the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council held in August 2026?
x: The 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting was held on 20 August 2026 in Tamil Nadu, chaired by Amit Shah.

s: On whose idea were the Zonal Councils set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
x: The Zonal Councils were the idea of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in 1956 and were set up in 1957.

s: For which projects did Telangana plan to seek national project status at the 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting (August 2026)?
x: At the 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting (Tamil Nadu, 20 Aug 2026), Telangana was to seek national status for Kaleshwaram and Palamuru-Rangareddy.

s: Under which law was the North Eastern Council set up?
x: The NEC is a statutory body under the North Eastern Council Act, 1971.

s: Which State became the eighth member of the North Eastern Council through the 2002 amendment?
x: The 2002 amendment added Sikkim as the 8th member State and made the NEC a regional planning body.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the North Eastern Council?
o: The Union Home Minister is its Chairman
The Minister of DoNER is its Vice-Chairman
The President nominates three of its members
It is a constitutional body under Article 263
x: The NEC is statutory, set up under the NEC Act, 1971, not a constitutional body.

s: Which of the following is a constitutional body?
x: The Inter-State Council rests on Article 263; Zonal Councils and the NEC are statutory and the NDC is non-statutory.

s: By what was the National Development Council, a non-constitutional and non-statutory body, created?
x: The NDC was created by an executive resolution, so it is neither constitutional nor statutory.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Inter-State Council is a constitutional body under Article 263, not a statutory one.

s: Which Article guarantees freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India?
x: Article 301 declares freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India, subject to the provisions that follow.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Articles 301 to 307?
o: Article 306 continues to operate as the principal provision for Part B States
Article 303 deals with preference or discrimination by the Union or States
Article 305 saves existing laws and State monopolies
Under Article 302, Parliament may restrict trade, commerce and intercourse in the public interest
x: Article 306, relating to Part B States, has been repealed.

s: A State Legislature proposes a bill imposing restrictions on trade, commerce or intercourse with other States under Article 304(b). What constitutional requirement applies before the bill is introduced?
o: Previous consent of the Supreme Court
x: A bill imposing reasonable restrictions in the public interest under Article 304(b) requires the previous sanction of the President before its introduction in the State Legislature.

s: Under Article 261(3), final judgments or orders of civil courts:
o: Can be executed only within the State concerned
Can be executed anywhere in India according to law
Need confirmation by the Supreme Court
Need the President's sanction for execution
x: Article 261(3) makes final civil court judgments and orders executable anywhere in India according to law.

s: Under Article 261(2), who decides the manner of proof of public acts and records and their effect?
x: Article 261(2) leaves the manner of proof and effect to Parliament by law.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides that full faith and credit shall be given to the public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and every State?
x: Article 261 is the full faith and credit clause.

s: The full faith and credit clause (Article 261) of the Indian Constitution is modelled on the Constitution of which country?
x: Article 261 is modelled on the Full Faith and Credit Clause of the US Constitution.

s: Which Article allows Parliament to restrict trade, commerce and intercourse in the public interest?
x: Article 302 lets Parliament impose restrictions in the public interest; Article 301 guarantees the freedom.

s: Which Article of Part XIII, relating to Part B States, has been repealed?
x: Article 306 on Part B States was repealed; Article 307 provides an authority for Articles 301-304.

s: Which provision lets Parliament bar the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts over inter-State river water disputes?
x: Article 262(2) lets Parliament bar court jurisdiction over water disputes, so Article 131 does not cover them; 262(1) provides for their adjudication.

s: Which Article of the Constitution gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction over disputes between the Union and States, but does not cover inter-State river water disputes?
x: Article 131 gives original jurisdiction; water disputes are excluded because Article 262(2) lets Parliament bar all courts.

s: In which year was the Vansadhara Water Disputes Tribunal constituted?
x: The Vansadhara Tribunal dates from 2010; the Godavari and First Krishna Tribunals from 1969 and the Second Krishna Tribunal from 2004.

s: The Mahadayi Water Disputes Tribunal (2010) involves Goa, Karnataka and which other State?
x: The Mahadayi Tribunal involves Goa, Karnataka and Maharashtra.

s: The Vansadhara Water Disputes Tribunal involves which States?
x: The Vansadhara Tribunal (2010) concerns Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.

s: Under Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, to whom does a State having a river-water dispute complain?
x: Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 provides for a State to make a complaint to the Central Government regarding an inter-State river-water dispute.

s: Which one of the following statements about the two 1956 laws is correct?
o: The River Boards Act created tribunals, while the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act created permanent river boards.
The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act provides for tribunals, whereas no board has ever been set up under the River Boards Act.
The River Boards Act repealed Article 262 and transferred water to the Union List.
Both laws provide only for advisory councils and neither concerns adjudication.
x: The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 provides for tribunals. Although the River Boards Act, 1956 provides a statutory framework for river boards, no board has ever been set up under it.

s: In which year was the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal set up?
x: The Cauvery Tribunal (Karnataka, Kerala, TN, Puducherry) was set up in 1990.

s: Under which law has no board ever been set up?
x: No board has ever been set up under the River Boards Act, 1956 (not 1970).

Match the following:
List-I (Tribunal)          List-II (Year set up)

x: Godavari 1969, Cauvery 1990, KWDT-II 2004 and Mahadayi 2010.

s: The Mullaperiyar dam on the Periyar is located in Kerala. Which State runs it under a lease?
x: The 1895 Mullaperiyar dam lies in Kerala but is operated by Tamil Nadu under a lease.

s: Which of the following States was NOT a party to the Narmada Water Disputes Tribunal set up in 1969?
x: The Narmada tribunal (1969) involved Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

s: Which of the following groups of water disputes tribunals involve Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh is a party to the Godavari, Krishna (I and II) and Vansadhara tribunals.

s: Under which Act were the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) and Godavari River Management Board (GRMB) set up?
x: KRMB and GRMB come from the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and work with an Apex Council.

s: At the January 2026 CWC-chaired inter-State meeting, what did Andhra Pradesh say about Telangana's 50:50 Krishna water demand?
o: is contrary to the KWDT awards and Apex Council decisions
should be settled jointly through the Zonal Council
should be referred to the Supreme Court
x: Andhra Pradesh rejected the 50:50 demand as contrary to the KWDT awards and the Apex Council's decisions.

s: What is the ad hoc division of Krishna water between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana from 2014-15?
x: KWDT-I's 811 tmcft for undivided AP is shared 512 (AP) : 299 (Telangana), a 66:34 ratio.

s: How much Krishna water did KWDT-I allot to undivided Andhra Pradesh?
x: KWDT-I allotted 811 tmcft to undivided AP; 968 tmcft is the Godavari figure AP disputes.

s: In which year did the Centre set the terms of reference for KWDT-II on the Krishna water dispute between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
x: The Centre set the terms of reference for KWDT-II on the AP-Telangana dispute in October 2023.
